intro.title: What I know how to do.
intro.kicker: Two halves of the same job. The technical work keeps a server stable, and the management work keeps it stable after I've left.

groups.title: Server configuration
groups.summary: Getting the platform right before a single plugin goes anywhere near it.

skills.name: Paper and Purpur tuning
skills.note: View distance, entity limits, chunk loading, and the handful of config flags that actually move tick time.

skills.name: Velocity and proxy networks
skills.note: Multi server routing, forwarding modes, shared player data, and restart cycles that don't kick anyone.

skills.name: World management
skills.note: Multiverse setups, pregeneration, borders, and seasonal world resets that don't lose builds.

skills.name: Performance profiling
skills.note: Reading Spark and timings reports properly, then fixing the cause instead of the symptom.

groups.title: Plugin configuration
groups.summary: Making twenty plugins behave like one system instead of twenty.

skills.name: LuckPerms architecture
skills.note: Inherited tracks, contexts and per server overrides that survive a rank rework.

skills.name: Economy and shop balancing
skills.note: Income sources paired with sinks, modelled up front rather than patched once inflation hits.

skills.name: Custom items and mobs
skills.note: ItemsAdder, MythicMobs and ModelEngine set up as one content pipeline.

skills.name: Config debugging
skills.note: Tracing conflicts between plugins that are quietly competing for the same events.

skills.name: Protection and logging
skills.note: WorldGuard regions, CoreProtect retention, and rollbacks that work when you're panicking.

groups.title: Discord engineering
groups.summary: Structure and automation for communities that outgrew one channel.

skills.name: Server architecture
skills.note: Channel trees, category permissions, and access that opens up as members stick around.

skills.name: Role and permission design
skills.note: Hierarchies that stay readable past thirty roles and never grant more than you meant.

skills.name: Bot configuration
skills.note: Verification, tickets, logging and auto moderation, all wired to a written rule set.

skills.name: Minecraft to Discord links
skills.note: Webhook relays for chat, punishments and rank sync across both platforms.

groups.title: Staff and team management
groups.summary: Building teams that make good calls with nobody watching.

skills.name: Hiring and rubrics
skills.note: Written application scoring, so hiring is repeatable instead of a gut feeling.

skills.name: Training and onboarding
skills.note: Two week onboarding with shadowing, checkpoints and an actual sign off at the end.

skills.name: Rotas and coverage
skills.note: Shift planning across timezones, with handover notes people genuinely read.

skills.name: Escalation and delegation
skills.note: Clear ladders, so every type of decision has a named owner and a fallback.

skills.name: Performance reviews
skills.note: Regular one to ones and honest feedback, well before a problem turns into someone quitting.

groups.title: Community operations
groups.summary: Policy and process that survive contact with a real argument.

skills.name: Rules and policy writing
skills.note: Rules specific enough to enforce the same way twice and defend in public.

skills.name: Conflict resolution
skills.note: De-escalation, mediation and appeals, without defaulting to whoever shouted loudest.

skills.name: Moderation systems
skills.note: Punishment ladders, appeal routes, and an audit trail for everything staff do.

skills.name: Retention and engagement
skills.note: Events and progression that bring players back without paying them to log in.

groups.title: Hosting and infrastructure
groups.summary: The unglamorous layer that decides how bad a bad night gets.

skills.name: Panel and host setup
skills.note: Pterodactyl nodes, allocations, resource limits, and restart schedules that make sense.

skills.name: Backups and recovery
skills.note: Offsite rotation, with restores that have actually been tested rather than just configured.

skills.name: Migrations
skills.note: Staged host and version moves with a rollback point at every step.

skills.name: Monitoring and alerting
skills.note: Uptime, tick rate and crash alerts going to whoever can actually do something about them.

toolbox.title: What I work with daily.
toolbox.kicker: Not a full list, just the things I reach for without thinking about it.

approach.title: How a job usually goes.
approach.kicker: Roughly the same whether it's one plugin misbehaving or a whole network rebuild.

steps.title: I look at what you've got
steps.body: Configs, plugins, roles, staff setup. Then I write down what's genuinely broken and what only looks messy, because those aren't the same thing.

steps.title: You get a plan first
steps.body: Before I touch anything you'll know what's changing, what's staying, roughly how long it takes, and what could go wrong along the way.

steps.title: Then I build it
steps.body: On a staging copy wherever that's possible, with checkpoints so you can see it coming together instead of waiting for a big reveal.

steps.title: And hand it over properly
steps.body: Written docs, a call with you and your staff, and two weeks of support afterwards. Ideally you never need to call me again.
